sections.title: Market Pulse: Stocks Drift Lower Amid Inflation Data and Nvidia Anticipation

items.headline: U.S. Stocks Edge Down on Wednesday as Investors Digest July Inflation Data and Await Nvidia Earnings
items.summary: Major U.S. indices traded lower today, pulling back from Tuesday's gains as the market reacted to July's Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index, which showed inflation was slightly higher than expected. Wall Street is also positioning ahead of key earnings reports, notably Nvidia's after the bell, which is seen as a bellwether for the AI sector. Bond yields remained relatively steady, while oil prices continued their recent decline.

items.headline: SolarEdge Technologies Up on Analyst Upgrade
items.summary: Shares of SolarEdge Technologies rallied after UBS upgraded the smart energy company's stock from Neutral to Buy, raising its price target.

items.headline: TTM Technologies Sees Significant Gains
items.summary: TTM Technologies, a leading global manufacturer of printed circuit boards, experienced notable upward movement today.

items.headline: Williams Companies Climbs on Natural Gas Demand
items.summary: Energy infrastructure company Williams Companies climbed, benefiting from surging natural gas demand driven by AI data centers and strong financial results.

items.headline: JinkoSolar Plunges on Q2 Earnings Miss
items.summary: JinkoSolar Holding Company Ltd. shares fell sharply after the company reported a miss on its second-quarter earnings and revenue estimates.

items.headline: Electromed Drops Despite Earnings Beat
items.summary: Electromed Inc. experienced a significant decline in share price despite reporting earnings that beat expectations for its fourth quarter.

items.headline: Dycom Industries Falls Despite Strong Infrastructure Demand
items.summary: Dycom Industries Inc. shares moved lower today, even as the company beat estimates on strong infrastructure demand.

items.headline: July PCE Inflation Rises More Than Expected, Heightening Fed Hike Chances
items.summary: The Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index, the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation gauge, increased 0.2% month-over-month in July and rose 3.7% year-over-year. This was slightly above economists' expectations, with the core PCE (excluding food and energy) holding steady at 3.3% year-over-year. The data has increased the perceived likelihood of a September Fed rate hike to 44%, up from 36% prior to the release.

items.headline: Q2 GDP Second Estimate Confirms Slower Growth at 1.5%
items.summary: The second estimate for the second quarter of 2026 real Gross Domestic Product (GDP) showed an annual growth rate of 1.5%, a slight downward revision from the advance estimate. This follows a 2.1% increase in the first quarter, with increased consumer spending and exports partially offset by a decrease in government spending.

items.headline: Nvidia Earnings Eyed After Market Close as AI Bellwether
items.summary: All eyes are on Nvidia ($NVDA) as the semiconductor giant prepares to report its fiscal second-quarter earnings after the market closes today. Analysts anticipate earnings per share around $2.09 on approximately $92.2 billion in revenue, with expectations extremely high given the company's pivotal role in the artificial intelligence investment cycle.

items.headline: Consumer Confidence Dips to Seven-Month Low in August
items.summary: Consumer confidence declined in August to a seven-month low of 89.4, falling 0.8% from the previous month and missing consensus estimates. This suggests a potential softening in consumer sentiment.

items.headline: Fed Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole Speech Anticipated for Policy Clues
items.summary: Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh is scheduled to deliver a keynote speech at the Jackson Hole Economic Policy Symposium on Friday, August 28. Market participants will be closely watching for any indications regarding the Fed's future monetary policy path, particularly in light of today's inflation data.
